scope.rescope: REWRITTEN 2026-07-30 for the 1774 Coercive-Acts slate. INTOLERABLE_ACTS and MERCANTILISM replaced the retired POSTWAR_REVENUE and STAMP_SCOPE; REPRESENTATION's six items are unchanged. This is the post-measure the lesson's four in-module checks are the baseline for: it re-asks the same three assessed concepts (both facets of INTOLERABLE_ACTS covered — the closure as collective punishment and the scope of the four acts) at matched difficulty with DIFFERENT items, which is the parallel-forms property the growth claim rests on.
scope.why: Under the M1-only freeze the other twenty-nine chapter concepts stay UNASSESSABLE: the gate is lenient for them by design, and no card of theirs mints. The registry declares Codex cards for exactly these three concepts and for no others.
scope.consequenceOfNarrowing: The chapter gate will pass a student who has mastered these three, and the report will say out loud that twenty-nine concepts were not asked. That is the honest state of the chapter, and the state the engine was built to survive. Under M1-only, these three concepts ARE the chapter.

met.how: Two items a form, three forms.
Exactly six items per concept, so three attempts each draw fresh items and nothing recycles. Eighteen items across the three concepts.
Three open-response items per concept, one per form.

met.requirement: `probe` distinct within a form; ITEM_PROBES has six stances and the reserve is six items
met.how: Each concept uses each of RECALL, BOUNDARY, ORDERING, CORRECTION, DISCRIMINATION and APPLICATION exactly once, so `probesDistinct` is true for every possible pair the shuffle can draw.

met.requirement: Provenance per item, never a blanket claim
met.how: Three released TEA items are mapped by reference in released-item-map.json; fifteen are authored and say so. No authored item claims a TEA administration.

met.requirement: No answer key in a descriptor
met.how: Keys live only in answer-key.json, and verify.mjs fails if a key-shaped field appears in an item file.
Every authored item carries 1774 or 1765; the two Intolerable-Acts released items are 1774 and the representation one 1765, all in window. verify.mjs re-runs the year-range parse @pa/curriculum uses.

divergences.topic: The open-response floor is three per concept, not one, and nothing in the package says so.
divergences.spec: `OPEN_RESPONSE_PER_FORM = 1` reads as one prose item per form.
divergences.judgement: Composed with `FRESH_FORM_TARGET = 3` and the quota being drawn fresh-first, it is a floor of THREE open-response items per concept. Worth stating in blueprint.ts next to the constant.

divergences.topic: INTOLERABLE_ACTS carries two released items, both selected-response.
divergences.spec: Nothing caps released items per concept.
divergences.judgement: Deliberate: the two measured coercion items (2021 #38, 2022 #4) are the evidence the concept was chosen against, so both are served. They take the RECALL and DISCRIMINATION probes, leaving the other four to authored items (one selected-response BOUNDARY, three open-response). It keeps the three-prose-per-concept floor and the six distinct probes.

perConcept.note: The three recognition-shaped stances (RECALL, BOUNDARY, ORDERING) take the selected-response slots and the three reasoning-shaped stances (CORRECTION, DISCRIMINATION, APPLICATION) take the prose slots. Two exceptions, both from released items: representation's released item is a DISCRIMINATION in selected-response form (so its authored RECALL takes an SR slot and ORDERING moves to prose), and Intolerable Acts' two released items are RECALL and DISCRIMINATION in SR form (so its authored ORDERING moves to prose).

BOS.CONCEPT.MERCANTILISM.v1.why: The one released mercantilism item (STAAR.2024.G8SS.37) is image-dependent and usableAsIs:false, so no released multiple-choice item on non-importation is servable. The same finding the retired STAMP_SCOPE carried; the six authored items carry the concept.

expectedReadiness.note: verify.mjs recomputes all of this with the same arithmetic blueprintReadiness uses, so the table is checked rather than claimed.

cardsThisUnlocks.note: Every Codex card the Boston registry declares hangs off these three concepts, so this eighteen-item pool is the whole of what stands between a student and a PvP-legal Codex.
